Watch out for those white moths. They lay eggs that hatch into those green caterpillars that will absolutely destroy your tomatoes and/or cannabis. I use Azamax to battle them if I get so many that I can't pull them off by hand fast enough.

I've had good success planting apiaceas(dill, fennel, caraway, celery left to flower, etc) very near my brassicas. The parasitic wasps wreck havoc on moth larva and especially aphids. The key is to plant multiple varieties of the apiaceas so there is constant flowering(dill flowers first, followed by cilantro, then caraway, then parsley root, then celery, then celeriac), and to give them a full year of no pesticides so they can develop a colony, usually with some sacrificial brassicas well away from your main crop.
